title: The Deep End
theme: The R&B records that lived below the radar — massive on the soul chart, largely invisible to pop audiences. The Persuaders, Latimore, Joe Simon, The Dells, Luther Ingram. Artists who built careers without crossover and songs that still hit harder than most of what surrounded them.
narrativePurpose: Test knowledge of the deep-catalog 1970s soul records that defined the genre for serious listeners — the labels, the songwriters, the artists, and the archival connections that reveal how wide and deep the era actually was.
toneProgression: The deep soul records that R&B fans know by heart → the labels, writers, and personnel stories behind the recordings → the archival connections that trace the reach of these overlooked classics

vault.note: Digit 4 (index 3) is always visible. Vault code 1-9-7-1 — the year 'Thin Line Between Love and Hate' (The Persuaders), 'Drowning in the Sea of Love' (Joe Simon), and 'The Love We Had (Stays On My Mind)' (The Dells) all appeared on the R&B charts — three deep soul records from the same twelve months, largely unknown to casual listeners. 1971: a year that lived in the deep end.

questions.question: Harold Melvin & The Blue Notes' 'If You Don't Know Me by Now' (1972) was later covered by which British soul-pop group, scoring a #1 hit in the United States in 1989?

metadata.artist: Harold Melvin & The Blue Notes / Simply Red
metadata.song: If You Don't Know Me by Now
topicTags: If You Don't Know Me by Now
metadata.fact: Simply Red's 1989 cover of 'If You Don't Know Me by Now' reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in the United States and #2 on the UK Singles Chart — their biggest US hit.
metadata.storyHook: A British soul-pop group took a Philadelphia classic to #1 in America seventeen years after the original. Harold Melvin didn't even make the Pop chart with it.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Simply Red's version reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1989 (not #1 UK — corrected from draft). Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_You_Don%27t_Know_Me_by_Now, Simply Red archive https://www.simplyred.com/archive/if-you-dont-know-me-by-now/

questions.question: Luther Ingram's 'If Loving You Is Wrong I Don't Want to Be Right' (1972) — one of soul music's most resigned forbidden-love anthems — was released on which Memphis-based label?

metadata.song: (If Loving You Is Wrong) I Don't Want to Be Right
metadata.fact: Luther Ingram recorded for KoKo Records, a small Memphis-based label with Stax affiliations. 'If Loving You Is Wrong' was produced by John Baylor and written by Homer Banks, Carl Hampton, and Raymond Jackson.
metadata.storyHook: KoKo Records. Memphis. A song about knowing something is wrong and not caring. Luther Ingram delivered it like he meant every word.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Luther Ingram recorded '(If Loving You Is Wrong)' for KoKo Records. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/(If_Loving_You_Is_Wrong)_I_Don%27t_Want_to_Be_Right

sources.title: (If Loving You Is Wrong) I Don't Want to Be Right – Wikipedia

questions.question: David Ruffin's 'Walk Away from Love' (1975) — his biggest solo hit — came after his departure from which iconic group where his voice had defined the sound?

metadata.fact: David Ruffin sang lead for The Temptations during their classic period before being fired in 1968. His solo career on Motown peaked with 'Walk Away from Love' in 1975.
metadata.storyHook: The voice of The Temptations went solo. It took seven years but 'Walk Away from Love' proved the voice was still everything.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: David Ruffin was best known as The Temptations' lead singer; fired 1968. Source: Classic Motown https://classic.motown.com/artist/david-ruffin/

sources.title: David Ruffin – Classic Motown artist bio

questions.question: The Main Ingredient's 1974 deep soul hit 'Just Don't Want to Be Lonely' was performed by Cuba Gooding — the father of which Oscar-winning actor?

metadata.song: Just Don't Want to Be Lonely
topicTags: Just Don't Want to Be Lonely
metadata.fact: Cuba Gooding (Sr.) was the lead singer of The Main Ingredient. His son Cuba Gooding Jr. won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for Jerry Maguire (1996).
metadata.storyHook: The singer's son won an Oscar. Cuba Gooding Sr. left something just as lasting — one of the smoothest soul ballads of 1974.

questions.question: The Persuaders' 1971 deep soul classic 'Thin Line Between Love and Hate' was released on which label — a subsidiary of Atlantic Records known for its soul and R&B catalog?

metadata.song: Thin Line Between Love and Hate
topicTags: Thin Line Between Love and Hate
metadata.fact: 'Thin Line Between Love and Hate' was released on Atco Records — Atlantic's subsidiary label — in 1971. The Persuaders were a Brooklyn-based duo who wrote, produced, and performed the song.
metadata.storyHook: Atco Records. Brooklyn. Two brothers who wrote the song, produced the song, and then sang it. The Persuaders did everything themselves.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Thin Line Between Love and Hate' released on Atco Records. Source: Spotify track metadata https://open.spotify.com/track/0hlthnSCTlKnRf91hR2f5L

questions.question: Lenny Williams' raw 1978 soul ballad ''Cause I Love You' became one of the era's most anguished vocal performances. Before his solo breakthrough, Williams had served as lead vocalist for which Oakland-based funk band?

metadata.fact: Lenny Williams is best known as Tower of Power's lead vocalist from the early 1970s. His visceral vocal style carried directly from that foundation into ''Cause I Love You.'
metadata.storyHook: He sang for Tower of Power. Then he went solo and made one of the most emotionally unguarded soul performances of the decade.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Lenny Williams was Tower of Power's lead vocalist. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenny_Williams

questions.question: Joe Simon's 1971 soul hit 'Drowning in the Sea of Love' was a Southern soul record — but the song was written and produced by which team best known for their Philadelphia International Records work?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 1 OF 3 — WRITTEN BY PHILADELPHIA'S FINEST

metadata.song: Drowning in the Sea of Love
topicTags: Drowning in the Sea of Love
metadata.fact: 'Drowning in the Sea of Love' was written and produced by Kenny Gamble and Leon Huff — the architects of Philadelphia International Records — despite being recorded by a Southern soul artist for Spring Records.
metadata.storyHook: Philadelphia's most famous producers wrote a record for a Southern soul singer on a New York label. The deep soul world didn't care about boundaries.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Drowning in the Sea of Love' written and produced by Kenny Gamble and Leon Huff for Spring Records. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drowning_in_the_Sea_of_Love, album entry https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drowning_in_the_Sea_of_Love_(album)

reserve.question: The Manhattans recorded 'Kiss and Say Goodbye' (1976) — their only #1 hit on the Billboard Hot 100 — for which major label?

metadata.fact: 'Kiss and Say Goodbye' was recorded for Columbia Records and released in 1976 as the lead single from the album The Manhattans — becoming the group's only #1 hit on the Billboard Hot 100.
metadata.storyHook: One #1 hit. One label. Columbia Records put 'Kiss and Say Goodbye' into homes across America in 1976.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Kiss and Say Goodbye' was released by Columbia Records in 1976. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_and_Say_Goodbye

reserve.question: Latimore — who released 'Let's Straighten It Out' in 1974 — built his career on which Miami-based independent label?

metadata.fact: Latimore built his career on Glades Records — a Miami-based soul imprint — releasing 'Let's Straighten It Out' in 1974 as part of a run of Southern soul recordings.
metadata.storyHook: Glades Records. Miami. And a voice so smooth it made working things out sound like the easiest thing in the world.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Latimore recorded 'Let's Straighten It Out' on Glades Records in 1974. Source: FleaMarketFunk https://fleamarketfunk.com/2010/05/11/latimore-lets-straighten-it-out/

reserve.question: The Manhattans — who recorded 'Kiss and Say Goodbye' — featured which vocalist as their primary lead singer throughout their commercial peak in the 1970s and 1980s?

metadata.fact: Gerald Alston was The Manhattans' principal lead vocalist from late 1970 through 1988, fronting the group through 25 Top 40 R&B hits including 'Kiss and Say Goodbye.'
metadata.storyHook: Gerald Alston fronted The Manhattans through 25 Top 40 R&B hits. The voice behind 'Kiss and Say Goodbye' — and most everything else they recorded in that era.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Gerald Alston was the Manhattans' lead singer between late 1970 and 1988. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Alston

questions.question: 'If Loving You Is Wrong I Don't Want to Be Right' was co-written by Homer Banks, Raymond Jackson, and Carl Hampton — the same songwriting team behind which 1968 Stax smash for Johnnie Taylor?

metadata.song: (If Loving You Is Wrong) I Don't Want to Be Right
metadata.fact: Homer Banks, Raymond Jackson, and Carl Hampton wrote both 'If Loving You Is Wrong' and Johnnie Taylor's 1968 Stax smash 'Who's Making Love' — establishing them as one of the Memphis soul era's most accomplished songwriting teams.
metadata.storyHook: Three writers. Two massive hits. Homer Banks, Raymond Jackson, and Carl Hampton built a catalog that went from Johnnie Taylor in 1968 to Luther Ingram in 1972.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Banks, Hampton, and Jackson wrote both songs. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/(If_Loving_You_Is_Wrong)_I_Don%27t_Want_to_Be_Right, Facebook story post https://www.facebook.com/ClassicCountryMusicStories/posts/the-story-behind-the-songif-loving-you-is-wrong-i-dont-want-to-be-righ

sources.title: (If Loving You Is Wrong) I Don't Want to Be Right – Wikipedia
'(If Loving You Is Wrong)' – writers Banks, Jackson & Hampton

questions.question: David Ruffin was fired from The Temptations in 1968 after increasingly erratic behavior. He was replaced as the group's lead vocalist by which singer?

metadata.fact: Dennis Edwards replaced David Ruffin as The Temptations' lead vocalist in 1968 and went on to front some of the group's most celebrated Norman Whitfield–produced psychedelic soul recordings.
metadata.storyHook: David Ruffin left. Dennis Edwards arrived. The Temptations didn't miss a beat — and then went somewhere entirely new.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Dennis Edwards replaced David Ruffin as Temptations lead vocalist in 1968. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Edwards

questions.question: The Dells — who recorded 'The Love We Had (Stays On My Mind)' in 1971 — released their major soul recordings on which subsidiary label of Chess Records?

metadata.song: The Love We Had (Stays On My Mind)
metadata.fact: The Dells recorded for Cadet Records — Chess Records' jazz and soul subsidiary — throughout their most commercially significant period of the late 1960s and early 1970s.
metadata.storyHook: Chess Records built an empire. Cadet was where they put the soul. The Dells found their most important recordings there.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: The Dells recorded for Cadet Records (Chess subsidiary) for their early-1970s releases. Source: AllMusic discography https://www.allmusic.com/artist/the-dells-mn0000130447/discography

questions.question: Latimore — associated with Miami soul — was actually born in which Southern state, a long way from the Florida scene where he built his career?

metadata.fact: Latimore (born Benjamin 'Benny' Latimore) was born in Charleston, Tennessee in 1939 — far from the Miami soul scene where he would eventually build his reputation on Glades Records.
metadata.storyHook: Charleston, Tennessee. Not Miami. Latimore came a long way to become the voice of Florida soul.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Latimore born Benjamin 'Benny' Latimore in Charleston, Tennessee. Source: FleaMarketFunk https://fleamarketfunk.com/2010/05/11/latimore-lets-straighten-it-out/

questions.question: 'Thin Line Between Love and Hate' was written and produced by two brothers who were also members of The Persuaders. What were their names?

metadata.song: Thin Line Between Love and Hate
topicTags: Thin Line Between Love and Hate
metadata.fact: Richard Poindexter and Robert Poindexter — brothers and members of The Persuaders — wrote and produced 'Thin Line Between Love and Hate,' with additional writing credit to Jackie Members.
metadata.storyHook: Two brothers. One song. Richard and Robert Poindexter wrote, produced, and performed 'Thin Line Between Love and Hate' — and made it feel like the most dangerous love story in soul music.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Richard and Robert Poindexter wrote and produced 'Thin Line Between Love and Hate' (with co-writer Jackie Members). Source: Spotify track credits https://open.spotify.com/track/0hlthnSCTlKnRf91hR2f5L

sources.title: Thin Line Between Love and Hate – song credits

reserve.question: Tower of Power — whose former lead vocalist Lenny Williams went on to record ''Cause I Love You' — were founded in which California city?

metadata.fact: Tower of Power were founded in Oakland, California — a city whose distinct R&B and funk scene gave the group a harder-edged, horn-driven sound unlike anything coming from Los Angeles.
metadata.storyHook: Not Los Angeles. Oakland. Tower of Power came from a tougher, rawer side of the California music scene.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Tower of Power founded in Oakland, California. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tower_of_Power

reserve.question: David Ruffin's 'Walk Away from Love' (1975) peaked at which position on the Billboard Hot 100 — his strongest solo chart performance?

metadata.fact: 'Walk Away from Love' reached #9 on the Billboard Hot 100 in early 1976 (following its 1975 release) — David Ruffin's best solo chart performance.
metadata.storyHook: Seven years after The Temptations. #9 on the Hot 100. David Ruffin proved he didn't need the group.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Walk Away from Love' reached #9 on the Billboard Hot 100. Source: Billboard chart history https://www.billboard.com/artist/david-ruffin/chart-history/hsi/

reserve.question: The Dells — one of R&B's longest-running vocal groups — were originally formed in which year?

metadata.fact: The Dells were formed in Harvey, Illinois in 1953 as a doo-wop group — going on to record and perform across multiple musical eras for over five decades.
metadata.storyHook: 1953. Harvey, Illinois. A doo-wop group that would still be recording decades later. The Dells outlasted almost everyone.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: The Dells formed in Harvey, Illinois in 1953. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dells

questions.question: The Persuaders' 'Thin Line Between Love and Hate' crossed genre lines when it was covered on which prominent British new wave act's 1984 album Learning to Crawl?

metadata.song: Thin Line Between Love and Hate
topicTags: Thin Line Between Love and Hate
metadata.fact: The Pretenders recorded 'Thin Line Between Love and Hate' for their 1984 album Learning to Crawl — one of the most unexpected genre crossings in the deep soul catalog's history.
metadata.storyHook: A Brooklyn soul record from 1971 ended up on a British new wave album in 1984. The Pretenders heard something in 'Thin Line' that transcended genre — and they were right.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: The Pretenders covered 'Thin Line Between Love and Hate' on Learning to Crawl (1984). Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Learning_to_Crawl

questions.question: The Dells — who recorded 'The Love We Had (Stays On My Mind)' in 1971 — are one of R&B's longest-running acts, having formed in 1953 in which Chicago suburb?

metadata.song: The Love We Had (Stays On My Mind)
metadata.fact: The Dells were formed in Harvey, Illinois — a Chicago suburb — in 1953. Their proximity to Chicago's gospel and doo-wop scenes gave them the foundation for one of the longest careers in R&B history.
metadata.storyHook: Harvey, Illinois. Not Chicago. Just outside. And yet The Dells became one of the city's — and the genre's — most enduring stories.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: The Dells formed in Harvey, Illinois in 1953. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dells

questions.question: Luther Ingram's 'If Loving You Is Wrong I Don't Want to Be Right' received a Grammy nomination at the 1974 Grammy Awards. In which category was it nominated?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 3 OF 3 — ITS GRAMMY NOMINATION CATEGORY

metadata.song: (If Loving You Is Wrong) I Don't Want to Be Right
metadata.fact: Luther Ingram's '(If Loving You Is Wrong) I Don't Want to Be Right' received a Grammy nomination for Best Rhythm & Blues Song at the 16th Annual Grammy Awards in 1974, covering 1973 releases.
metadata.storyHook: A KoKo Records record on a small Memphis label got a Grammy nomination for Best Rhythm & Blues Song. The Academy noticed what soul fans already knew.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Grammy nomination for Best Rhythm & Blues Song at the 16th Grammy Awards (1974). Source: Grammy.com https://www.grammy.com/awards/16th-annual-grammy-awards

reserve.question: Joe Simon — who recorded 'Drowning in the Sea of Love' in 1971 — was born in Simmesport in which Southern state?

metadata.fact: Joe Simon was born in Simmesport, Louisiana — a Southern gospel background that informed the devotional intensity of his soul recordings.
metadata.storyHook: Simmesport, Louisiana. A small town that produced one of the era's most emotionally charged soul voices.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Joe Simon born in Simmesport, Louisiana. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Simon_(musician)

reserve.question: Latimore's Glades Records was a subsidiary of which larger Miami-based independent operation — run by entrepreneur Henry Stone — that dominated Florida's soul output throughout the 1970s?

metadata.fact: Glades Records was one of several subsidiary labels run by Henry Stone under the TK Records umbrella — the Miami operation that also launched KC and the Sunshine Band on the disco side of its catalog.
metadata.storyHook: Henry Stone ran TK Records. Glades was where he put the soul. KC and the Sunshine Band were next door — and Latimore was the deep end of the catalog.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Glades Records was a TK Records subsidiary under Henry Stone. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TK_Records, FleaMarketFunk https://fleamarketfunk.com/2010/05/11/latimore-lets-straighten-it-out/
